title: Specified projection components under localization and coefficient-field towers
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t$; put $A_n=R/(t^n)$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum], not a datum assuming projection invertibility. Schemes are finite type over $k$ and their structure morphisms need not be separated. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories and the specified compactification projection map [def-exchange-projection], with compact-support functors [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type. For integral bounded constructible $K_0,L_0$ in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] with $L_0$ finite Tor, let $Q$ be raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Under the canonical operation comparisons the rational component at $QK_0,QL_0$ is precisely $Q(\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_0,L_0})$. For every finite coefficient-field extension $E\subset F$ inside a fixed $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, the specified scalar-extension functors and their tensor, pullback and compact-support comparisons identify the extension of this very component with the component at $F$; they also identify the defining units, counits and open tensor maps. These identifications satisfy the identity and tower cocycles. Consequently, for two inputs represented over a common finite field, these components define one morphism in the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], independently of further enlargement. If the integral component is invertible, its rational inverse is $Q(\operatorname{PF}^{-1})$, and any common-stage representative of its scalar extension has inverse represented by that extended inverse. The same comparisons carry naturality and any equality between the specified composites to the field stages. No finite reduction of a rational object without an integral representative is claimed.

proof.text: Represent the source and target endpoint isomorphisms as components of the composites of the recorded natural comparisons. Private component-formula lemmas prove equality with the original ordered component formulas. Use the projection comparison field of SixFunctorExchangeComparison in the supplied operation datum. Postcompose its equation with the inverse of its final comparison, then cancel the source comparison. This gives transported = projectionComponent for any coefficient comparison, hence for rationalization, finite coefficient extension and common-stage inclusion. No invertibility hypothesis is used.

Composition and Cartesian products preserve the component identity and tower equations of ExchangeProjectionScalarCocycle. Prove this by naturality of the second comparison and functoriality of its operation. Apply these calculations to support times identity followed by tensor, and to identity times pullback followed by tensor and support. SixFunctorCommonStageCoherence supplies support and pullback equations and the equivalent scalar-cocycle representation of TensorCoherence supplies tensor equations. These give both endpoint cocycles, including identity inclusions.

The analogous composition and product calculations for SixFunctorInclusionCoherence follow from functoriality and naturality of the second inclusion comparison. Apply them to the same endpoint factorizations, with the operation datum supplying pullback/support inclusion equations and TensorCoherence supplying tensor inclusion equations. This proves InclusionCoherence.

Uncurry the natural transformation stage.projection and transport its source and target by the recorded operation equalities. This gives naturality for arbitrary arrows in every supplied category, and naturality at the inclusion transition isomorphisms gives EnlargementLaw after replacing transported components by the first step. Transport inverse equations by functoriality and cancel adjacent endpoint isomorphisms. An equality is carried forward simply by substituting its two equal maps. Assemble the ten conjuncts.
